relationships.note: Raised in the same workshop street; they disagree like two hands of the same craft.

characters.silhouette: A tall hooded figure with square shoulders, a long apron of carved panels and a hem that widens like a tree root.

story_arc.summary: A-Mu finds the kiln cold for the first time in living memory and assumes the fire guardian has abandoned the village.
A-Mu refuses to finish a commissioned panel because the grain needs fire to set the inlay; the buyer walks away.
A-Mu walks to the kiln with a half-carved panel, and the two guardians build one bench where wood and fire are finished together.

taboos: never cuts a living tree for a commission
never signs a piece that a craftsperson did not finish

voice.signature_line: Measure twice, and let the wood keep the second measure.

characters.archetype: restless maker who listens to the kiln

relationships.note: Trusts the wood guardian's patience but not the silence that came with it.

story_arc.summary: A-Huo let the fire die to keep the forest from being cut for a season, and cannot explain the choice without sounding like a refusal.
A single test tile survives the cold kiln with a crackle no one has seen; A-Huo realises the village glaze was waiting for this.
A-Huo carries the kiln fire to the wood bench and teaches the finishing step to the village apprentices, finishing A-Mu's half-carved panel.

taboos: never fires a glaze that copies a protected ritual object
never sells a second firing without telling the buyer

voice.signature_line: The kiln does not argue; it answers in colour.

title.en: The Two Guardians of the Craft Village

world.conflict: The kiln guardian has let the fire grow cold to protect the forest, and the wood guardian reads that silence as betrayal; the village loses its glaze and the two stop speaking.
world.premise: A craft village lives by two promises: the forest gives the wood, the kiln gives the colour. Two guardians keep the promises, and when one of them stops listening the village loses half of what it knows.
world.resolution_theme: The two crafts are one practice: the wood needs the fire to finish it, and the fire needs the wood to be worth burning.
rules: A guardian may borrow a motif from the village, but may never claim a traditional prototype as private property.
Every piece made under a guardian's name carries the name of the craftsperson who finished it.
When a guardian takes, the guardian must also teach; craft knowledge never leaves the village without a student.

setting.en: A craft village between a mountain range and a bay. By day the woodworking and jewellery workshops share one street; by night the kiln fire and the mountain wind take turns watching over the village. Two guardians are said to keep it: one of timber and grain, one of kiln fire and glaze.
setting.zh: 群山与海湾之间的一个手艺村。白天，木作与首饰工坊共用一条街；夜里，窑火与山风轮流守着村子。传说有两位守护者，一个守着木材与纹理，一个守着窑火与釉色。
